correctness.rationale: A half-turn conjugates the two signs of Omega. For r=|Omega|/b, zeros of the derivative are intersections of g(t)=cos(t)(r-sin(t)) with the negative level -1/(4 pi a b^2). Differentiation gives g'=2 sin^2(t)-r sin(t)-1, and the only possible stationary sines are u_− and u_+. The negative lobe at u_− persists for every r; the one at u_+ requires r<1. At a stationary sine u, the absolute depth is (1-u^2)^(3/2)/|u|, strictly decreasing in |u|, so the primary well is strictly deeper except at symmetry. Each negative lobe has one strict nondegenerate minimum, with g''=q sqrt(1-u^2); its two monotone sides give exactly the stated counts and multiplicities. The lift is strictly increasing even at a=a1 because its nonnegative derivative has only isolated zeros. A negative derivative arc above a1 precludes injectivity for a degree-one circle map. Expansion u_+=1-(1-r)/3+O((1-r)^2) gives both edge constants; Taylor expansion at each minimum gives the pair separation sqrt(2 depth/g'') sqrt(epsilon)/pi in the relative parameter epsilon. The threshold formulas are analytic in the reduced variable r on their finite branches. As functions ordered by onset in signed Omega, they have a cusp at zero; the analytic sheets exchange order there. The bundled script was inspected, not executed, and is not an exhaustive parameter argument.
residual_risks: No inference about chaos or entropy above the first threshold.
